citation: Iyengar N, Peng CK, Morin R, Goldberger AL, Lipsitz LA. Age-related alterations in the fractal scaling of cardiac interbeat interval dynamics. Am J Physiol 1996;271(4):R1078-R1084. Fantasia Database, PhysioNet (Goldberger et al. 2000).
record_used: subject f1y01 (young healthy adult), the first 5-minute RR window (time <= 300 s, 391 RR intervals) -- the SAME git-tracked Fantasia RR the sibling HRV-DFA case uses. The young-vs-old panel uses all 10 subjects (f1y01-05 young, f1o01-05 old), each first 5-min window.
pipeline: readRDS(rr_fantasia) -> first-5-min window (Task Force short-term HRV) -> PhysioECG::ecgHRVpoincare: the Poincare-plot descriptors SD1 (short-term/beat-to-beat RR variability, a parasympathetic proxy), SD2 (long-term variability, analytical closed-form SD2^2 = 2*SDNN^2 - 0.5*SDSD^2), and their ratio. The reference re-computes them with an independent from-scratch numpy implementation of the analytical closed-form (bit-exact) and cross-checks NeuroKit2 hrv_nonlinear (SD1 bit-for-bit; NeuroKit2's SD2 = geometric paired-projection, reproduced bit-for-bit by an independent numpy paired projection). Deterministic.
note: The tracked input is agent/eval/data/hrv-dfa/rr_fantasia.rds (Fantasia RR); the fold's certified root is its f1y01 first-5-min window (agent/eval/data/poincare-hrv/rr5min_f1y01.rds). The Poincare plot (RR_n vs RR_n+1) is the classic nonlinear-HRV geometry: SD1 = the cloud's width perpendicular to the identity line (short-term/vagal variability), SD2 = its length along the line (long-term variability). ecgHRVpoincare reproduces an independent from-scratch numpy analytical closed-form BIT-FOR-BIT (max |diff| 0 over SD1/SD2/ratio) and NeuroKit2 hrv_nonlinear: SD1 bit-for-bit (SD1 = SDSD/sqrt(2) is universal); SD2 up to a documented ~0.196 ms (~0.24%) convention -- the op uses the analytical closed-form, NeuroKit2 the geometric paired-projection std((RR_n+RR_n+1)/sqrt(2)), which an independent numpy paired projection reproduces bit-for-bit, so the gap is a convention choice (equivalent in the large-n limit), NOT an error. The finding: short-term HRV (SD1) is markedly higher in the young (mean 53.1 ms) than the old (35.3 ms) -- an age-related decline in cardiac-vagal variability, the GEOMETRIC complement of the DFA aging result (alpha1 rises with age) on the same Fantasia cohort. Descriptive on n=5+5 subjects, one database.
